question: What is the success rate and token cost of the COLD baseline (no registry) on the synthetic 32-task corpus using a real LLM, and does this viability close the token-based inheritance economics line?
hypothesis: The COLD baseline (no registry) achieves >= 90% success rate with average token cost <= 100 tokens/task on the synthetic 32-task corpus, making token-based parameterized inheritance unnecessary because the cheapest baseline is already viable.
falsifier: COLD success rate < 90% OR average token cost > 150 tokens/task, indicating that COLD is not viable and registry-based inheritance may still be needed.

baselines.description: No registry. Real LLM generates the correct URL from the task goal without any mechanism guidance via API call.
baselines.expected_behavior: Single LLM call generates URL from task description only; no selection or resolution overhead; success rate measured (not assumed).

baselines.description: Full literal registry (32 concrete-URL mechanisms). Real LLM selects from all 32 mechanisms via API call; executes the matched mechanism directly.
baselines.expected_behavior: Reference baseline for token cost comparison; not primary target.

baselines.description: Deduplicated parameterized registry (25 mechanisms with ${slot} templates). Real LLM selects from 25 mechanisms via API call and resolves the matched template via a second API call.
baselines.expected_behavior: Reference baseline for token cost comparison; not primary target.

positive_control.description: The 5 blog-read-post tasks (simple GET /posts/{id}) must be solvable by COLD with correct URL generation.
positive_control.expected_behavior: All 5 tasks produce correct URLs under COLD; success rate 100% on these simple tasks.

null_control.description: Tasks with complex parameters (admin, auth, search) may have lower COLD success rate, indicating registry value.
null_control.expected_behavior: COLD success rate on complex tasks may be lower than on simple tasks; not required to pass.

measurement_validity: Both conditions use the identical 32-task synthetic corpus from parent EXP-PRODUCT-35330741529 (6 domains, 32 tasks)
All token counts measured from real LLM API calls via tiktoken on actual prompt+completion text, not estimated
COLD step: single API call with task description only; model outputs URL
Success rate measured per-task: resolved URL matches expected URL exactly
Each task executed independently; no cross-task state contamination
Temperature 0.0 for deterministic output; API model specified in provenance
Registry text format identical to parent (numbered list of [METHOD] URL pattern) for reference baselines
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of: (C1) COLD success rate >= 90% across all 32 tasks; (C2) average COLD token cost (prompt+completion) <= 100 tokens/task; (C3) positive control passes (5 blog-read-post tasks succeed). FALSIFIED if any condition fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if API failures prevent completion of >=5 tasks.
product_consequence_positive: If COLD achieves >=90% success with <=100 tokens/task, token-based inheritance economics are closed: the cheapest baseline is viable, and parameterized inheritance adds net token overhead without必要 benefit. Product lane pivots to alternative mechanisms (registry compression, retrieval efficiency, orthogonal capabilities). C-PRODUCT-ECON advances toward REJECTED for token-based savings.
product_consequence_negative: If COLD fails (<90% success or >150 tokens/task), registry-based inheritance may still be needed. The parent's 5.42% analytical savings remain potentially relevant, and the product lane should pursue option A (re-run with API keys) or option B (real SPIDER corpus). C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS.
estimated_cost: Low — 32 tasks × 1 condition × 1 LLM call each = 32 API invocations. At ~500 tokens/call average ≈ 16K total tokens. No browser/network execution needed.
expected_information_gain: High — directly resolves whether COLD baseline is viable, which determines whether token-based inheritance economics are worth pursuing. A positive result (COLD viable) closes the line; a negative result (COLD not viable) keeps it open. Both outcomes materially change the C-PRODUCT-ECON claim or product decision.
